question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 2 Model Practice Paper (Journey of a River)

questions.question_text: Where does the river Godavari originate?
questions.correct_answer: B) Trimbakeshwar in Western Ghats

questions.question_text: India's national aquatic animal, the Ganges river dolphin, navigates muddy river waters using:
questions.correct_answer: B) Echolocation (ultrasonic sound waves)

questions.question_text: What type of landform is created when a slow-moving river deposits fine silt near its ocean mouth?
questions.correct_answer: C) River delta

questions.question_text: Which river in Rajasthan is an inland drainage river that terminates in the Rann of Kutch salt marsh?
questions.correct_answer: B) Luni

questions.question_text: What is a primary economic benefit of constructing large dams across major rivers?
options: B) Stores water in reservoirs for irrigation and generates hydroelectric power
questions.correct_answer: B) Stores water in reservoirs for irrigation and generates hydroelectric power

questions.question_text: Trace the journey of a river from its mountain origin to its ocean mouth, highlighting changes in velocity and landforms.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Mountain Course: Steep slope, high water velocity, cuts V-shaped valleys and gorges through heavy bed erosion. 2) Plains Course: Moderate/flat slope, water slows down, widens, forms meanders and alluvial plains. 3) Ocean Mouth: Very slow velocity, deposits carried silt to form fan-shaped fertile river deltas.

questions.question_text: Describe the unique adaptation of the Ganges river dolphin for survival in turbid river waters.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The Ganges river dolphin is blind due to murky river waters. It emits high-frequency ultrasonic clicks (echolocation) that bounce off objects, fish, and riverbeds. By interpreting returning sound echoes, it constructs a mental spatial map to navigate, avoid obstacles, and hunt prey.

questions.question_text: Comprehensive Analysis of River Systems: Explain river course landforms, dam trade-offs, and ecological restoration efforts in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Landforms: Mountain erosion creates V-shaped gorges and waterfalls; plains deposition forms meanders and fertile alluvial plains; mouth siltation forms river deltas (e.g., Sundarbans). Dam Trade-offs: Dams provide irrigation, flood control, and hydroelectricity, but submerge forests, disrupt migratory fish (like Mahseer), and displace communities. Restoration: Initiatives like Namami Gange combine industrial effluent treatment, municipal sewage treatment plants, afforestation along riverbanks, and public awareness to preserve river health.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Fishermen along a stretch of the Ganga river reported that catches of fish had dropped by 80% following the construction of a chemical factory upstream and a dam downstream. Q1: What two distinct factors harmed the fish population? Q2: What corrective measures under Namami Gange can restore fish stocks?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Q1: Factor 1 - Toxic chemical effluent from the factory depleted dissolved oxygen and poisoned fish. Factor 2 - The dam created a physical barrier blocking migratory fish pathways and altering downstream water flow. Q2: Corrective measures: Enforce zero liquid discharge on the chemical factory with strict water treatment, and construct fish ladders/passes at the dam site while releasing environmental water flow.

questions.correct_answer: B) Slows down significantly

questions.question_text: Why is the Ganges river dolphin blind?

questions.question_text: What ecological drawback is associated with building large river dams?
options: B) Submerges upstream forests and displaces local wildlife and human settlements
C) Causes rain to stop in oceans
questions.correct_answer: B) Submerges upstream forests and displaces local wildlife and human settlements

questions.question_text: Discuss two major positive benefits and two negative impacts of constructing large river dams.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Positive Benefits: 1) Stores massive water reservoirs for agricultural irrigation during dry seasons. 2) Generates clean hydroelectricity without burning fossil fuels. Negative Impacts: 1) Submerges vast upstream forest ecosystems and agricultural land. 2) Displaces indigenous human settlements and disrupts fish migration pathways.

questions.question_text: How does the Namami Gange programme address Ganga river pollution?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Sewage Treatment: Building modern treatment plants to treat domestic sewage before discharge. 2) Industrial Effluent Monitoring: Regulating factories along riverbanks to stop toxic chemical dumping. 3) Riverfront Development & Biodiversity Conservation: Protecting aquatic species like dolphins and turtles while promoting public sanitation.

questions.question_text: Detail the biological characteristics, ecological role, and conservation threats facing the Ganges River Dolphin.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Biological Characteristics: National aquatic animal of India, locally called 'Susu'. Blind by evolutionary adaptation to turbid waters, relies on ultrasonic echolocation to navigate and hunt. Ecological Role: Apex predator in Ganga-Brahmaputra river ecosystem; presence indicates healthy water quality and rich fish biodiversity. Conservation Threats: 1) Water pollution from industrial chemicals and sewage, 2) Entanglement in nylon fishing nets, 3) Dam/barrage barriers fragmenting dolphin populations and reducing water flow.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Farmers in a village near the Aravalli hills depend on a local seasonal river for well recharge. In recent years, sand mining along the riverbed removed all natural sand layers, leaving bare rock. During monsoons, rainwater rushed past rapidly without recharging wells. Q1: Why did sand removal stop well recharge? Q2: How can natural riverbed management restore groundwater?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Q1: Riverbed sand acts as a natural sponge, slowing down water flow and allowing rainwater to soak into the underground aquifer. Bare rock surfaces cause water to rush past rapidly as surface runoff without soaking in. Q2: Stop illegal sand mining, construct small check-dams (johads) across the stream to slow water flow, and restore vegetation along riverbanks.

options: A) A canal dug by humans
B) A smaller stream or river that flows into a larger main river
questions.correct_answer: B) A smaller stream or river that flows into a larger main river

questions.question_text: Fine soil and organic particles transported and deposited by flowing river water are called:
questions.correct_answer: B) Alluvial silt

questions.question_text: What happens to river water carrying capacity when its speed decreases on flat plains?
options: B) It loses kinetic energy and deposits carried sediments
questions.correct_answer: B) It loses kinetic energy and deposits carried sediments

questions.question_text: Which region of India is known as the origin point for major east-flowing rivers like Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery?
questions.correct_answer: B) Western Ghats

questions.question_text: What is an estuary?
options: A) High mountain peak where snow melts
B) Coastal area where a river's freshwater meets and mixes with ocean salt water
questions.correct_answer: B) Coastal area where a river's freshwater meets and mixes with ocean salt water

questions.question_text: Explain why the Luni river is classified as an inland drainage river.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Unlike major peninsular rivers that empty into open oceans (Bay of Bengal or Arabian Sea), the Luni river originates in the Aravalli range in Rajasthan and flows through arid terrain, eventually terminating and losing its flow in the marshy salt flats of the Rann of Kutch without reaching any sea.

questions.question_text: Why are river deltas exceptionally fertile and suitable for agriculture?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: As rivers slow down near their mouth, they deposit fine alluvial silt, mineral-rich sediments, and organic matter accumulated along their entire journey. This creates flat, nutrient-dense delta soil (like the Sundarbans) ideal for intensive crop cultivation.

questions.question_text: Analyze the hydrological differences between east-flowing and west-flowing peninsular rivers in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: East-flowing rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery, Mahanadi): Originate in Western Ghats, flow across gentle eastern plateau gradient, form extensive fertile deltas before entering Bay of Bengal. West-flowing rivers (Narmada, Tapti): Flow through steep rift valleys between Vindhya and Satpura ranges, high velocity, empty into Arabian Sea forming narrow estuaries rather than deltas.

questions.question_text: Case Study: A town located on a river bank experienced severe annual flooding after upstream forests were cleared for timber. Silt levels in the river rose dramatically, making the river shallow. Q1: How did deforestation upstream cause the river bed to rise? Q2: What dual solution can reduce flood risks?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Q1: Deforestation exposed soil to erosion; rain washed loose soil into the river (siltation), filling the riverbed and reducing water holding capacity. Q2: 1) Replant trees along upstream catchments and riverbanks to bind soil. 2) Desilt the river channel to restore depth.

options: B) Introduces toxic chemicals that kill aquatic life and deplete dissolved oxygen
C) Causes rivers to flow backward

questions.question_text: Which national water animal is locally known as 'Susu' due to the noise it makes while breathing?
questions.correct_answer: B) Ganges river dolphin

questions.question_text: How do tree roots on riverbanks protect against severe flood damage?
options: A) They absorb all flood water completely
B) They bind bank soil together and reduce water erosion speed
C) They turn river water into salt
questions.correct_answer: B) They bind bank soil together and reduce water erosion speed

questions.question_text: The delta formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers before entering the Bay of Bengal is called:
questions.correct_answer: B) Sundarbans Delta

questions.question_text: How does deforesting riverbanks worsen flood damage and river siltation?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Tree roots bind riverbank soil. Deforestation exposes loose soil to fast water currents, causing bank erosion. Eraded soil accumulates on the riverbed (siltation), raising bed height, reducing channel capacity, and causing water to overflow banks easily during heavy monsoons.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between perennial rivers and seasonal (rain-fed) rivers with examples.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Perennial Rivers (e.g., Ganga, Yamuna): Originate from melting Himalayan glaciers and snowmelt, maintaining continuous water flow throughout the year. Seasonal Rivers (e.g., Luni, many peninsular streams): Rely solely on monsoon rainfall and dry up or shrink significantly during summer months.

questions.question_text: Examine the environmental impacts of sand mining and riverbed alteration on river ecosystems.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Impacts: 1) Instability: Sand removal collapses riverbanks and undermines bridge piers. 2) Water Quality: Turbidity increases, choking fish gills and blocking sunlight. 3) Groundwater Depletion: Loss of porous riverbed sand reduces natural aquifer recharge. Restoration requires strict regulation, sustainable alternatives, and riverbank afforestation.

questions.question_text: Case Study: A conservation team monitored a Ganges river dolphin population trapped between two dam barrages. Over 5 years, dolphin numbers declined due to net entanglement and reduced water depth in dry months. Q1: How do dams fragment aquatic animal populations? Q2: What management strategy protects trapped dolphins?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Q1: Dams act as impassable barriers, isolating small populations, restricting gene flow, and trapping dolphins in shallow river segments during summer. Q2: Maintain minimum environmental water releases from barrages, enforce dolphin-safe fishing nets, and establish protected river sanctuaries.

B) The entire geographical area drained by a main river and all its tributaries
D) A water tank on a building roof

questions.question_text: How does water pollution affect dissolved oxygen levels and aquatic animal survival in rivers?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Chemical pollutants, untreated sewage, and agricultural fertilizers cause excessive algal blooms (eutrophication). When algae die, decomposing bacteria consume dissolved oxygen in water, creating hypoxic dead zones where fish and dolphins suffocate.

questions.question_text: Explain how river water is diverted for human agricultural use through canal networks.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Dams or barrages built across rivers hold back water, raising water level. Controlled sluice gates release water into main irrigation canals. These branches spread across dry agricultural plains, supplying water directly to crop fields miles away from the main river.

questions.question_text: Discuss the role of rivers in human settlement history, agricultural development, and cultural traditions in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Settlements: Ancient Indian civilizations (Indus Valley, Vedic sites) grew along riverbanks due to accessible freshwater and fertile soil. Agriculture: Rivers feed canal networks powering India's food production. Culture: Rivers like Ganga, Godavari, and Narmada are revered in festivals, literature, and art as vital lifelines.

questions.question_text: Case Study: A coastal village at a river delta observed that mangrove forests along the coast were being cut for hotel construction. During the next cyclone, storm surges flooded farmlands with salt water. Q1: What protective role did mangrove forests play? Q2: Why is delta ecosystem conservation critical?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Q1: Dense mangrove root systems break the energy of tidal storm surges, act as natural windbreaks, and prevent coastal soil erosion. Q2: Delta mangroves shelter young marine fish, protect inland communities from sea flooding, and filter river sediments.
